title: C4OS Grill Question 050 - Plugin Migration Failure Handling

questions.label: Which plugin migration failures should C4OS automatically recover from?
questions.help: Recommended: auto-recover only mechanical/local-state issues such as cache rebuilds, missing installed copies that can be reinstalled from a known source, and stale indexes; visibly disable security, incompatibility, dependency, or native binding failures.
options: Auto-recover cache, reinstallable bundle, and stale-index failures only
Auto-recover any failure where C4OS can infer a fix
Never auto-recover; visibly disable on all migration failures
Ask the user before every migration recovery attempt

questions.label: Which plugin migration failures should cause visible disablement instead of recovery?
questions.help: Select all failure classes that should leave the plugin visible in Settings with a disabled state and reason.
options: Missing marketplace source or non-reinstallable plugin bundle

questions.label: How should C4OS handle corrupt plugin-owned user config during migration?
questions.help: Recommended: keep a backup of the corrupt config, disable only the affected plugin, and show repair/reset actions in Settings.
options: Back up corrupt config, disable affected plugin, and show repair/reset actions
Reset corrupt plugin config automatically and keep plugin enabled
Block app startup until user fixes the config
Ignore corrupt plugin config and use plugin defaults silently

questions.label: Where should migration failures be surfaced to the user?
questions.help: Recommended: Settings > Plugins for durable state, plus a startup notification only when user action is needed.
options: Settings > Plugins with disabled reason and repair actions
Startup notification only when user action is needed

questions.label: Notes or corrections
questions.help: Add any correction to the recommended policy or any migration failure case that is missing.
